title: Reinforcing Diffusion Models by Direct Group Preference Optimization
abstract: Direct Group Preference Optimization (DGPO) is an online reinforcement learning method for post-training diffusion models. It keeps the group-relative preference signal that makes GRPO useful, but removes the need for stochastic SDE policy rollouts by learning group-level preferences directly in a DPO-style objective. This enables deterministic ODE rollouts, avoids full-trajectory policy-gradient training, and yields around 20x faster training than Flow-GRPO while improving GenEval, OCR text rendering, PickScore alignment, and several out-of-domain reward metrics.
publication_status: Accepted as poster at ICLR 2026; arXiv preprint also available.

openreview.note: Reviewers praised the clear motivation, 20-30x faster training, strong benchmark performance, and evaluation. Main concerns involved novelty relative to DPO/GRPO, missing derivation details, beta/group-size/timestep-clip sensitivity, comparison to concurrent DiffusionNFT, reward quality, CFG, and PPO-style clipping.
